Honda Civic Buyer's Guide

2 generations, 3 body styles, a 49-mpg hybrid, the Si and 2 Type Rs. Which Civic to buy used, and what to check before you pay.

By Celia Marchetti · 6 chapters, about 21 min in all · Updated November 17, 2026 · Find one for sale

In this guide
  1. ●Overview
  2. 12017–2021
  3. 22022–2026
  4. 3Hybrid
  5. 4Si
  6. 5Type R
  7. 6Used checklist

The Civic is the car most Americans picture when they think of Honda, and between 2017 and 2026 it came in more forms than ever. The tenth generation, sold here through 2021, offered a sedan, a coupe and a hatchback built in England, plus the first Civic Type R sold new in the US. The eleventh generation, from 2022, dropped the coupe, moved hatchback production to Indiana and, for 2025, added a 200-hp hybrid rated at up to 49 mpg. The Si and the Type R run alongside both generations, with a year off each.

For a used buyer, the choices are the generation, the body, the engine and, for the Si and Type R, how the car has been driven. This guide has 6 chapters: one for each generation, one each for the Hybrid, the Si and the Type R, and the checklist to use before you buy. We've combined our separate sedan, coupe and hatchback reviews into the generation chapters, because those bodies share their engines, cabins and recalls.

Quick picks

  • Best all-rounder: a 2025 or later Civic Hybrid, with 200 hp and an EPA rating of up to 49 mpg combined.
  • Best value: a 2019–2021 Civic sedan with the 2.0-liter engine. Honda Sensing is standard, and it's rated at 33 mpg.
  • Most practical: a Civic hatchback, either generation, for its big rear opening and folding seat.
  • Best to drive on a budget: a 2017–2020 or 2022 and later Civic Si, with a 6-speed manual and a limited-slip differential.
  • The real performance car: a 2017–2021 or 2023 and later Type R. Car and Driver ran both from 0 to 60 mph in 4.9 seconds.
  • Think twice if you want an automatic Si or Type R, or all-wheel drive. Neither exists.

The chapters

Chapter 1The Civic That Stopped Apologizing2017–2021 · Tenth generation · Sedan, coupe and hatchback

A low, sharp-steering compact with a rear seat adults can use, in 3 body styles. The most plentiful used Civic, and one of the best.

4 min readChapter 2The Civic Grows Up2022–2026 · Eleventh generation · Sedan and hatchback

Calmer to look at, nicer to sit in and still sharp to drive. Just know which engine you're buying, because Honda changed them for 2025.

3 min readChapter 3The Quickest Civic Short of a Type R2025–2026 · Civic Hybrid · Sedan and hatchback

200 hp, up to 49 mpg and no plug to worry about. Car and Driver found it quicker to 60 mph than the Si.

3 min readChapter 4The Civic You Have to Shift Yourself2017–2020 and 2022–2026 · Civic Si · Sedan and coupe

A 6-speed manual, a limited-slip differential and a chassis that rewards a good driver. Not the quickest Civic any more, and that isn't the point.

3 min readChapter 5Front-Wheel Drive, No Apology2017–2021 and 2023–2026 · Civic Type R · FK8 and FL5

A 306-hp, then 315-hp, front-drive hatchback with a manual gearbox, that runs to 60 mph in 4.9 seconds. How to find one that hasn't been abused.

3 min readChapter 6Buy the Civic, Not the Reputation2017–2026 · The used Civic checklist

A good reputation can't undo a missed oil change or a hidden accident. How to confirm which Civic you're looking at, what to check, and how to judge the price.
